case_title: West Nile neuroinvasive disease presenting as acute flaccid paralysis during late pregnancy
source_title: West Nile virus presenting as flaccid paralysis: Case report and literature review

confirmatory_evidence: Aseptic CSF pleocytosis with mixed neutrophil/lymphocyte differential
Brain MRI T2/FLAIR signal in bilateral caudate nuclei, putamen, and posterior thalamus
Spine MRI with prominent ventral cauda equina nerve-root enhancement
Clinical acute asymmetric flaccid paralysis with altered mental status
case_quality.boundary_notes: This is WNND with acute flaccid paralysis and radicular imaging, not Guillain-Barre syndrome, epidural abscess, isolated viral meningitis, or nonspecific postpartum weakness.

demographics.pregnancy_context: 39 weeks pregnant at symptom onset, delivered by Cesarean section before transfer

time_anchor.day0_definition: Transfer evaluation with altered mental status, fever, worsening ascending paresis, CSF review, and brain/spine MRI

risk_context.source_text_value: At symptom onset she was 39 weeks pregnant and delivered a healthy term baby by Cesarean section before transfer.
Right leg paresis progressed to both legs, right upper extremity, and face with severe lower extremity weakness.

presentation_summary: 21-year-old woman at 39 weeks pregnancy developed low back pain and insomnia two weeks before transfer, followed by gradually worsening right leg paresis.
After Cesarean delivery at an outside hospital, paresis spread to both lower extremities and ascended to involve the right upper extremity and face.
She developed fever and worsening altered mental status before transfer.
Exam showed somnolence, inability to follow commands, and severe lower-extremity weakness worse on the right.
CSF had 46 nucleated cells with 59% neutrophils, 30% lymphocytes, and 11% macrophages; protein was normal and glucose was elevated.
Brain MRI showed bilateral caudate, putamen, and posterior thalamic T2/FLAIR hyperintensity without diffusion restriction or abnormal enhancement.
Spine MRI showed prominent enhancement of ventral cauda equina nerve roots without cord compression, cord signal abnormality, or cord enhancement.
Toxicology and heavy-metal screens were negative; CSF bacterial, acid-fast, fungal cultures and HSV, CMV, and enterovirus testing were negative; CSF WNV IgM was positive.
She improved with supportive care but had residual lower-extremity weakness and was discharged to inpatient rehabilitation.

observations.source_text_value: Low back pain developed two weeks before transfer.
Fever was present but no numeric temperature was reported.
Altered mental status worsened; exam showed somnolence and inability to follow commands.
Severe asymmetric lower extremity weakness, worse on the right, with ascending involvement.
Worsening right-sided hemiparesis and asymmetric flaccid paralysis of extremities.
Ascending paresis with ventral cauda equina root enhancement.
Paresis ascended to involve the face, but detailed cranial nerve localization was not provided.
CSF had 46 nucleated cells with mixed inflammatory differential.
A serology test was positive for WNV IgM in CSF.
Brain MRI showed bilateral caudate nuclei, putamen, and posterior thalamus T2/FLAIR signal.
MRI showed bilateral caudate nuclei and putamen involvement.
Spine MRI showed prominent enhancement of ventral nerve roots of the cauda equina.
Weakness was progressive and ascending before diagnosis.
She retained residual lower-extremity weakness and needed inpatient rehabilitation.

time_series.source_text_value: Severe lower-extremity weakness worse on the right, with right upper extremity and facial involvement.

imaging.finding: Normal head CT, limited by motion
imaging.source_text_value: Contrast-enhanced CT of the head was normal, although limited by motion.

imaging.finding: T2/FLAIR signal in bilateral caudate nuclei, putamen, and posterior thalami without diffusion restriction or enhancement
imaging.source_text_value: Brain MRI demonstrated increased T2/FLAIR signal in bilateral caudate nuclei and putamen as well as posterior thalamus; no diffusion restriction or abnormal parenchymal/leptomeningeal enhancement.

imaging.finding: Prominent ventral cauda equina nerve-root enhancement without cord compression or cord signal abnormality
imaging.source_text_value: Spine MRI showed prominent enhancement of ventral nerve roots of cauda equina, with no extrinsic compression, abnormal signal, or enhancement of the spinal cord.

diagnostics.source_text_value: The case report did not describe EEG findings.
Comprehensive toxicology and heavy-metal screening had negative results.
Spine MRI demonstrated no extrinsic compression.

microbiology.source_text_value: A serology test was positive for WNV IgM in CSF, identifying the causative agent.

microbiology.test: CSF bacterial, acid-fast, and fungal cultures
microbiology.source_text_value: No bacterial, acid-fast, and fungal organisms grew in CSF cultures.

microbiology.test: CSF HSV, CMV, and enterovirus serology tests
microbiology.source_text_value: CSF serology tests for herpes simplex virus, cytomegalovirus, and enterovirus were negative.

clinical_course_events.source_text_value: Two weeks before transfer, while 39 weeks pregnant, she developed low back pain and insomnia.

treatments.dose_or_context: Empiric antiviral and antibiotic medications before transfer
Discharged to inpatient rehabilitation for residual lower-extremity weakness

outcome.neurologic_outcome: Improved after supportive care but retained residual lower-extremity weakness and was discharged to inpatient rehabilitation; no later follow-up was available.
outcome.pregnancy_outcome: Delivered a healthy term baby by Cesarean section before transfer; the report did not identify apparent neonatal complications.
outcome.mortality_hazard_relevance: Severe acute flaccid paralysis and encephalopathy raised disability and respiratory-risk concern, but no death or ventilatory failure was reported.

case_boundary_warnings: The pregnancy and Cesarean delivery are host/context facts, not disease-name qualifiers.

Ventral cauda equina root enhancement plus acute flaccid weakness should be consumed as WNND motor-neuron/radicular expression, not as spinal epidural abscess because there was no compression or abscess.
CSF protein and glucose were qualitative only; no numeric values were invented.
